2609_05312v1.summary: Analysis of 20 JWST/NIRSpec PRISM transits of LP 890‑9b and c reveals timing shifts that suggest a third planet, LP 890‑9d, with an orbital period near 4.4 days.
highlights: Peak‑to‑peak TTV amplitudes reach ~17 s for b and ~35 s for c
Two‑planet models cannot reproduce the observed TTV super‑period
Three‑planet fits place a candidate LP 890‑9d between b and c

2609_04308v1.headline: Supernova Microlensing Offers New Window onto Ultracompact Minihalos and Primordial Power
2609_04308v1.summary: A proposed method uses LSST supernova microlensing to detect ultracompact minihalos, linking their abundance to constraints on the early‑Universe power spectrum.
highlights: Supernova microlensing can reveal lenses up to ~pc scales for masses around 10^4 M⊙
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s LSST will provide a massive supernova sample for this search
Projected limits on minihalo abundance translate into bounds on small‑scale primordial power

inflows_galaxies_2026.headline: DESI Survey Finds Inflows in Up to Half of Galaxies, Revealing Baryonic Cycling
inflows_galaxies_2026.summary: A new analysis of ~30,000 galaxies using DESI spectroscopy shows coherent inflowing gas at ~100 km/s in 20‑50% of the sample, overturning expectations about gas flows in star‑forming versus quiescent systems.
highlights: Inflows detected in 20‑50% of galaxies, including many quiescent types
Star‑forming galaxies mainly exhibit bound outflows, suggesting a galactic fountain recycling on ~0.5 Gyr
Detected inflows are metal‑rich, implying recycled halo gas rather than pristine accretion

2609_04597v1.headline: NASA's Habitable World Observatory Could Detect Ocean Glint on Earth‑Like Exoplanets
2609_04597v1.summary: Simulated observations show that a phase angle of at least 120° and signal‑to‑noise ratios between 5 and 25 enable reliable detection of ocean glint signatures.
highlights: Glint detection requires phase angles ≥120°
Signal‑to‑noise ratios of 5–25 are sufficient for retrievals
Model selection confirms glint presence over non‑glint models

rapid_quenching_protocluster_z2_2.headline: Gas‑depleted, quenched galaxies discovered in the Spiderweb protocluster at z = 2.16
rapid_quenching_protocluster_z2_2.summary: A stacked analysis of HST, JWST and ALMA data reveals massive galaxies in the Spiderweb core that stopped forming stars about 500 Myr ago and retain less than 7 % of their gas.
highlights: Stacked HST F160W, JWST Paβ imaging and ALMA 1.2 mm data constrain star‑formation histories and gas content
Average gas fraction fgas < 7 % for the quiescent population
Rapid quenching occurred ≈500 Myr before observation, matching progenitor HAEs

2609_04313v1.headline: Environmental Multitracer Method Boosts Primordial Non‑Gaussianity Constraints for DESI LRGs
2609_04313v1.summary: A new technique that splits galaxy samples by large‑scale dark‑matter environment halves the uncertainty on local‑type primordial non‑Gaussianity, reaching σ(f NL)≈1.
highlights: Multitracer analysis uses dark‑matter environment instead of halo mass or secondary properties
Validated with N‑body and Quijote simulations showing unbiased f NL recovery
DESI LRG forecasts predict a 2‑3× improvement over single‑tracer methods

2609_04991v1.headline: New Method Refines Dark Siren Cosmology and Updates Hubble Constant Measurement
2609_04991v1.summary: Researchers introduce a sampled redshift prior to jointly infer galaxy host properties and cosmology, yielding H₀ = 71.9⁺⁹·¹₋⁷·⁵ km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹.
highlights: Joint inference of host‑galaxy weighting model achieved for the first time
Updated Hubble constant value aligns with previous GWTC‑5.0 results
Method mitigates galaxy catalogue incompleteness and redshift uncertainties

2609_04312v1.headline: ALPACA Pipeline Cuts JWST Lens Modeling Time to Hours, Controls PSF Systematics
2609_04312v1.summary: A new GPU‑accelerated pipeline, ALPACA, jointly reconstructs source galaxies and PSF for JWST lensing, reducing runtimes to under 15 hours while keeping H₀ bias below one percent.
highlights: ALPACA reduces per‑system modeling time from weeks to <15 hours using GPU acceleration
Joint source‑pixel and PSF reconstruction limits DΔt bias to the percent level
Validated on realistic JWST/NIRCam mock data built from COSMOS galaxies

2609_05128v1.headline: Isolated Binary Evolution Could Yield Unequal‑Mass Black‑Hole Mergers With High‑Spin Primaries
2609_05128v1.summary: Researchers propose two isolated‑binary pathways that may produce unequal‑mass binary black‑hole mergers featuring a primary black hole spinning near 0.7, challenging the need for hierarchical mergers.
highlights: Mass‑ratio reversal in wide binaries can spin up and enlarge the second‑born black hole
Chemically homogeneous evolution of a close primary star can create a massive, high‑spin first‑born black hole
Large natal kicks or tertiary‑induced Kozai‑Lidov oscillations can generate significant spin‑orbit misalignments

2609_04334v1.headline: BAO Data Point at z = 0.706 Drives Dark‑Energy Tension in Predictive Tests
2609_04334v1.summary: A leave‑one‑redshift‑block cross‑validation shows that a single DESI DR2 BAO measurement, not supernovae, favors evolving dark energy over ΛCDM.
highlights: ΔELPD scoring finds modest preference for w₀wₐCDM driven by BAO
The LRG2 block at z = 0.706 supplies the entire BAO preference
All SNIa datasets show ΔELPD consistent with zero, indicating no predictive tension

2609_05230v1.headline: ALMA Detects Gas Gaps and Kinematic Signatures Linked to Giant Protoplanets in WISPIT 2 Disk
2609_05230v1.summary: High‑resolution ALMA observations reveal co‑located gas gaps and rotation anomalies in the WISPIT 2 protoplanetary disk, matching the positions of previously imaged giant protoplanets.
highlights: Gas gaps appear in the 12CO integrated intensity map and its rotation curve
The gaps exhibit eccentric shapes consistent with massive planet‑disk interaction models
An outer disk lacking eccentricity suggests a third unseen planet may be present

immune_aging_mice.headline: Blocking EP2 Receptor Reverses Aging Signs in Mice
immune_aging_mice.summary: A Stanford study published in Science shows that disabling the EP2 receptor in tissue‑resident macrophages restores youthful inflammation patterns and improves memory, frailty, muscle and heart function in older mice.
highlights: EP2 signaling was blocked using drugs and genetic editing in aged mice
Restored clearance of senescent neutrophils by tissue‑resident macrophages
Observed improvements in memory, frailty, muscle mass and cardiac performance

quantum_phases_chromium_spin_triplet.headline: Three distinct spin‑triplet phases discovered in potassium chromium arsenide
quantum_phases_chromium_spin_triplet.summary: Researchers at Okayama University identified three spin‑triplet superconducting phases in K₂Cr₃As₃, revealing topological properties and potential for fault‑tolerant quantum computing.
highlights: Three superconducting phases (A, B, C) appear under different magnetic‑field strengths applied along the crystal c‑axis
Phase B breaks time‑reversal symmetry while Phase C hosts a line node in the superconducting gap
The material’s transition temperature is 6.2 K, the highest reported for a spin‑triplet superconductor
Nuclear magnetic resonance was essential for probing spin susceptibility in the superconducting state

shmr_dwarf_desi_dr1.headline: DESI Data Release 1 Extends Stellar‑to‑Halo Mass Relation into Dwarf Galaxy Regime
shmr_dwarf_desi_dr1.summary: Using DESI DR1, researchers map the stellar‑to‑halo mass relation down to galaxies with stellar masses below 10⁹ M⊙, revealing steeper slopes and larger scatter at dwarf scales.
highlights: DESI Bright Galaxy Survey provides clustering, lensing, and satellite occupation measurements for 12 stellar‑mass samples
Average halo‑to‑stellar mass relation follows log⟨M_h⟩=12.06+0.58 log(M_★/10¹¹)+(M_★/10¹¹)^0.73
Power‑law slope of the SHMR steepens from 0.32 ± 0.06 at Milky Way masses to 2.08 ± 0.21 in dwarf galaxies
Scatter in the SHMR grows from 0.17 dex to 0.68 dex when moving from Milky Way‑like to Large Magellanic Cloud‑like systems

noise_entanglement.headline: Noise‑Engineered Entanglement Links Distant Qubits Without Active Pulses
noise_entanglement.summary: Researchers at ISTA demonstrated that correlated microwave noise can autonomously entangle two transmon qubits over a metre, offering a continuous‑time quantum link.
highlights: Entanglement achieved using a Josephson parametric converter that splits pump photons into correlated gigahertz pairs.
Two transmon qubits separated by a metre of coaxial cable settle into a dark entangled state while the field remains on.
The protocol requires no synchronized pulses, heralding, or feedback, reducing overhead for scalable quantum networks.
Measured concurrence is 0.10, representing about ten percent of the original continuous‑variable entanglement.

gaia_quiet_bh_discoveries.headline: Quiet Black Holes with Stellar Companions Challenge Formation Theories
gaia_quiet_bh_discoveries.summary: Three silent stellar‑mass black holes identified by Gaia’s precise astrometry reveal unexpected close companions, prompting new questions about their binary formation pathways.
highlights: Gaia detected three inactive black holes by observing stellar wobbles without seeing a luminous companion
Two systems (BH1 and BH2) have unusually close orbits despite the progenitor star’s expansion
Roche Lobe Overflow may allow mass transfer without merging, preserving the binary
The study is based on a peer‑reviewed paper in the Astrophysical Journal (2026)

dwarf_agn_jwst_nirspec.headline: JWST NIRSpec Uncovers Varied Nuclear Environments in Dwarf AGN Hosts
dwarf_agn_jwst_nirspec.summary: Using JWST/NIRSpec IFU, astronomers mapped the central kiloparsec of four dwarf galaxies, finding over 100 emission lines and diverse gas and dust signatures.
highlights: Over 100 emission lines detected, including coronal lines with ionization potentials >300 eV
Hot dust contributes strongly to the infrared continuum in two of the galaxies
PAH and coronal line emission observed within 100 pc of the nuclei in three galaxies
Hot H₂ gas mass estimated at 1–20 M⊙ within 300 pc, showing both thermal and non‑thermal excitation

shared_genetic_roots_ocd_tourette_autism.headline: Rutgers Team Identifies 36 Shared Risk Genes Linking OCD, Tourette and Autism
shared_genetic_roots_ocd_tourette_autism.summary: A new Nature Neuroscience study expands known high‑confidence genes to 36, revealing strong genetic overlap among OCD, chronic tic disorders and autism.
highlights: 36 genes now linked to OCD and chronic tic disorders, many also associated with autism and schizophrenia
Risk variants can increase disease odds up to 210‑fold, with an average 57‑fold effect
Analysis of nearly 4,000 cases—including 2,400 parent‑child trios—highlights the cortico‑striato‑thalamo‑cortical circuit

reversible_electric_control_chiral_phono.headline: Electric Field Switches Handedness of Chiral Phonons in BaTiO₃ Device
reversible_electric_control_chiral_phono.summary: Researchers demonstrated that a reversible 3 V electric field can flip and retain the chirality of phonons in a 40 nm BaTiO₃ membrane at room temperature.
highlights: Chiral phonon handedness reverses when the ferroelectric polarization of BaTiO₃ is switched
The switched state persists after the electric field is removed
Circularly polarized X‑rays at ESRF were used to read phonon chirality via RIXS

desi_dr11.headline: DESI Legacy Imaging Survey Unveils 5.6‑Trillion‑Pixel 2D Cosmic Map
desi_dr11.summary: The DESI Legacy Imaging Survey’s 11th data release presents a 5.6‑trillion‑pixel map of nearly 4 billion objects, covering 75 % of the sky.
highlights: The map contains ~4 billion stars, galaxies, quasars and asteroids across 75 % of the sky.
Data were captured with DECam on the 4‑meter Mayall telescope, the 2.3‑meter Bok telescope, and NASA’s WISE.
The release supports DESI’s goal to build the largest high‑resolution 3D map for dark‑energy studies.
More than 160 scientists contributed, linking the survey to upcoming Rubin and Roman observatories.

deep_biosphere_persistence.headline: Deep Biosphere Survived Caledonian Mountain Building and Erosion for 378 Million Years
deep_biosphere_persistence.summary: Microbial methanogenesis persisted in a 2.3‑km deep Swedish borehole, with episodic activity spanning from 378 million to 1.8 million years ago.
highlights: Mineral‑scale carbon isotope signatures reveal ancient methane‑producing microbes
U–Pb dating links microbial bursts to major tectonic uplift and erosion events
Study based on fracture‑filling calcite from the COSC‑2 drill core in central Sweden

selfprocessingbrain_jneurosci_2026.institution: Institute of Biophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
selfprocessingbrain_jneurosci_2026.headline: Self‑Processing Brain Networks Show Conservation and Reorganization Across Primates
selfprocessingbrain_jneurosci_2026.summary: Researchers compared structural and gene‑expression data in humans, chimpanzees and macaques, finding conserved interoceptive circuits but divergent abstract self‑processing pathways.
highlights: Small‑scale brain structure and gene expression are highly similar between humans and macaques
Large‑scale connectivity reveals chimpanzees as an intermediate between macaques and humans
Interoceptive processing aligns macaques with chimpanzees, while exteroceptive processing aligns chimpanzees with humans
Abstract mental self‑processing shows the greatest species differentiation

climate_amplifies_earthquakes_arctic.headline: Climate Change Amplifies Earthquake‑Triggered Avalanches on Jan Mayen’s Permafrost‑Bound Slopes
climate_amplifies_earthquakes_arctic.summary: A 6.5‑magnitude quake on Jan Mayen in March 2025 caused a rock avalanche, with warming‑induced permafrost loss making the volcanic slope unusually vulnerable.
highlights: The March 10 2025 quake (M 6.5) triggered a massive rock avalanche on the Kjerulf Glacier
Permafrost thaw reduced ice cement that stabilised the volcanic slope of Beerenberg
Satellite data showed unprecedented debris spread and calving at neighboring Weyprecht Glacier
Study published in PNAS demonstrates climate‑driven amplification of seismic hazards in the Arctic

scientists_observe_einstein_s_gravity_in.headline: Einstein’s Equivalence Principle Holds for Falling Quantum Atoms in First Direct Test
scientists_observe_einstein_s_gravity_in.summary: Physicists used ultracold rubidium atoms in a Quantum Galileo Interferometer to directly observe the predicted quantum phase shift under gravity, confirming Einstein’s principle at the quantum level.
highlights: Quantum phase shift measured matches Einstein’s equivalence principle prediction
Experiment split rubidium atom wave into stationary and free‑falling paths using magnetic fields
Team included Nobel‑winning Sir Roger Penrose and researchers from Ben‑Gurion University, Oxford and Ulm

hubble_webb_tno.headline: Hubble and Webb Reveal Tiny TNOs Preserve Early Solar System Secrets
hubble_webb_tno.summary: Joint Hubble‑Webb observations of 27 ultra‑faint Trans‑Neptunian Objects show they retain the same colors and size distribution as larger siblings, challenging collision models.
highlights: 27 new TNOs detected, including one as faint as fireflies on the Moon
Smallest observed TNO measures ~5 km (3 mi) in diameter
Both hot and cold TNO populations share identical color‑size relationships

early_statin_dementia_risk.headline: Early Statin Use Cuts Dementia Risk by 15% in Diabetics
early_statin_dementia_risk.summary: A Danish cohort of 132,585 newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients showed a 15 % lower dementia risk over ten years when statins were started within one year.
highlights: Statin initiation within one year of diagnosis reduced dementia risk by 15 % relative to no early treatment
Starting statins between one and five years after diagnosis still lowered risk, but by only 10 %
Only 2.7 % of participants developed dementia during a median 7.1‑year follow‑up

glueball_candidate_decay.headline: BESIII Finds Strongest Evidence Yet for Long‑Sought Glueball X(2370)
glueball_candidate_decay.summary: Using 10 billion J/ψ decays, BESIII researchers identified X(2370) as a glueball‑dominated particle, noting a missing kaon‑pair decay that supports its gluon‑only nature.
highlights: X(2370) spin‑parity matches predictions for the lightest glueball.
The kaon‑pair decay channel is limited to ≤8 % of the dominant decay mode.
Analysis used the full 10 billion J/ψ dataset from the BEPCII collider.
Results are presented in a preprint on arXiv and at the International Conference on High Energy Physics.

personality_gwas_big5.headline: Over 1,200 Genetic Variants Linked to Big Five Personality Traits
personality_gwas_big5.summary: An international consortium identified more than 1,200 DNA variants associated with the Big Five traits, revealing extensive genetic ties to health, income and lifestyle outcomes.
highlights: 1,200+ variants correlate with openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism
Combined genetic effects are sizable despite tiny individual impacts
Same variants predict personality across ages and continents

gut_asthma_connection.headline: Gut‑Linked Immune Shifts Found in Fatal Asthma Cases
gut_asthma_connection.summary: A study of 695 organ donors reveals that fatal asthma attacks involve heightened type‑2 inflammation and altered immune cells in gut‑associated lymph nodes.
highlights: All 41 fatal‑asthma donors had IgE levels above the reference threshold
Lung tissue showed increased type‑2 helper T cells, innate lymphoid cells, and mast cells
Gut‑associated lymph nodes displayed stronger immune connections than in non‑asthma donors

moon_formation_impact_2026.headline: Temperature-Dependent Material Strength Alters Moon Formation in New Impact Simulations
moon_formation_impact_2026.summary: New SPH simulations show that hotter, weaker Theia leads to an intact Moon, while cooler, stronger Theia produces a debris disk, reshaping giant impact models.
highlights: Hot, weak Theia yields an intact Moon within five hours of impact
Cool, strong Theia generates a classic protolunar debris disk
Inclusion of temperature‑dependent material strength changes momentum transfer and accretion percentages
Simulations align with prior models for hot collisions but diverge for cool scenarios

rattlesnake_antivenom_discovery.headline: Rattlesnake Blood Yields Antivenom Ten Times More Potent Than Current Treatment
rattlesnake_antivenom_discovery.summary: Researchers combined rattlesnake serum proteins to create an antivenom that proved about ten times more effective than existing commercial snakebite therapy in lab tests.
highlights: Combination of FETUA proteins blocked lethal effects of multiple viper venoms
Optimized protein mixtures were ~10‑fold more potent than sheep‑derived antivenom
Study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2026

copd_late_stage_trial.headline: AstraZeneca’s tozorakimab cuts COPD flare‑ups by 30% in Phase 3 trials
copd_late_stage_trial.summary: Late‑stage Phase 3 studies show AstraZeneca’s injectable drug tozorakimab reduces COPD exacerbations by roughly 30% over a year, offering a new therapeutic option.
highlights: tozo lowered COPD exacerbations by about 30% across all patients
Phase 3 trials included participants ineligible for existing COPD drugs
Results presented at the European Respiratory Society conference in Barcelona and published in the New England Journal of Medicine

fast_growing_blackholes_2026.headline: eROSITA Finds Eight Supermassive Black Holes Growing Ten Times Faster Than Their Galaxies
fast_growing_blackholes_2026.summary: A new eROSITA survey of over 20,000 quasars reveals eight black holes that comprise about 5 % of their host galaxies’ mass and may double in size within a billion years.
highlights: Eight quasars show a black‑hole‑to‑galaxy mass ratio of ~20 : 1 instead of the typical ~200 : 1
These over‑massive black holes account for roughly 5 % of their galaxies’ total mass
Three of the eight are among the brightest quasars, indicating extreme accretion rates
The study used eROSITA X‑ray data combined with optical/infrared galaxy brightness measurements

siberian_methane_regimes_2026.headline: Arctic warming splits Siberia into wet and dry methane‑emitting regimes
siberian_methane_regimes_2026.summary: Rising Arctic temperatures are creating contrasting climate regimes in western and eastern Siberia, driving a 5% annual rise in methane emissions from the region.
highlights: Western Siberia’s wetlands are getting wetter, boosting microbial methane release from thawing permafrost
Eastern Siberia is drying, increasing wildfire‑driven methane emissions
Methane emissions grew by about 13.2 million tons between 2010‑2023, a 5% yearly increase
Satellite‑based methane flux inversion limited estimate uncertainty to roughly 10%

sparse_data_sst_method.headline: Sparse-data method boosts global sea surface temperature estimates by 40%
sparse_data_sst_method.summary: A new Sparse Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method (S-DEIM) predicts sea surface temperatures 40% more accurately than traditional DEIM and outperforms top AI models.
highlights: S-DEIM achieved 40% higher accuracy than the classic DEIM approach
S-DEIM was 2% more accurate than the best‑performing convolutional neural network
Training time dropped from 1½ hours to one minute
The test used 30 years of NOAA SST observations, withholding the final year for validation

rewired_ribosomes.headline: Engineered Ribo‑M Ribosomes Dedicated to Single‑Protein Production
rewired_ribosomes.summary: University of Illinois Chicago scientists have created Ribo‑M, a ribosome permanently linked to its mRNA, enabling focused synthesis of one protein.
highlights: Ribo‑M physically links a ribosome to its messenger RNA, eliminating the search for genetic instructions
The platform successfully produced fluorescent, antibiotic‑resistance, and light‑emitting proteins in bacterial tests
Future designs aim to incorporate non‑canonical amino acids for more stable therapeutic proteins

antibiotic_efflux_mechanism.headline: University of Osaka uncovers new fosfomycin efflux pump in Streptococcus pneumoniae
antibiotic_efflux_mechanism.summary: Researchers identified the ABC transporter FoeAB that actively exports fosfomycin, revealing a novel resistance mechanism in the pneumonia‑causing Streptococcus pneumoniae.
highlights: The previously unknown ABC transporter FoeAB increases bacterial resistance when overexpressed.
Cryogenic electron microscopy captured FoeAB in open‑inward and open‑outward conformations.
FoeAB was reconstituted in artificial membranes, directly demonstrating fosfomycin transport.
Fosfomycin is added to the list of antibiotics known to be expelled by bacterial efflux pumps.

vicarious_calibration_fengyun3.headline: Vicarious Calibration Boosts Accuracy of Fengyun‑3D/F Ocean Color Data
vicarious_calibration_fengyun3.summary: A new vicarious calibration model dramatically reduces radiometric bias in FY‑3D and FY‑3F MERSI sensors, enabling reliable quantitative ocean color measurements.
highlights: Calibration model corrects biases in FY‑3D and FY‑3F ocean color channels
Ground‑based observations and radiative transfer simulations underpin the method
Improved remote‑sensing reflectance supports global carbon sink monitoring

plant_co2_response_drylands.headline: Rising CO₂ Slows Projected Expansion of Global Drylands
plant_co2_response_drylands.summary: A new study shows that plant water‑use reductions under higher CO₂ limit dryland growth, cutting projected expansion by up to 2 percent of land by 2100.
highlights: Drylands currently cover 38.58% of Earth's land, excluding Antarctica
Including CO₂‑induced plant effects reduces the high‑emissions scenario projection from 42.11% to 40.28% of land
Regional shifts are pronounced, with drying risks in Australia, eastern Brazil and northern Africa

heatwaves_antibiotic_resistance_soils.headline: Heat Waves Slash Soil Antibiotic Resistance but Damage Ecosystems
heatwaves_antibiotic_resistance_soils.summary: Extreme heat waves temporarily reduce soil antibiotic resistance genes, yet cause severe damage to soils and ecosystem functions across Europe.
highlights: Heat waves caused a marked drop in antibiotic resistance gene abundance in soils from cold, wet regions
Soils from warm, dry countries showed greater resilience to heat and drought stress
Geography proved the strongest predictor of resistance gene levels, outweighing the type of extreme event

proto_supercluster_distance_record.headline: Record‑breaking proto‑supercluster COSMOS‑z3.1‑A discovered at 2.1 billion‑year age
proto_supercluster_distance_record.summary: An international team using DECam and DESI mapped the distant proto‑supercluster COSMOS‑z3.1‑A, revealing a structure 5,000 times the Milky Way’s mass when the universe was only 2.1 billion years old.
highlights: COSMOS‑z3.1‑A is the earliest and most massive proto‑supercluster ever observed
The ODIN survey’s DECam imaging enabled identification of 150 protoclusters, with 3‑D mapping via DESI, GMOS and DEIMOS
The structure’s mass exceeds that of the local Coma Cluster by a large margin

black_hole_growth.headline: Overmassive Black Holes Outpace Their Host Galaxies, Study Finds
black_hole_growth.summary: A new eROSITA survey of over 20,000 quasars reveals eight black holes whose masses constitute about 5 % of their galaxies, growing far faster than typical.
highlights: Eight quasars show a black‑hole‑to‑galaxy mass ratio of roughly 20 : 1 instead of the usual 200 : 1
Three of these overmassive black holes are among the brightest X‑ray sources in the sample
The authors estimate such black holes could double their mass within a billion years

trees_buffer_animals.headline: Tree Cavities Buffer Extreme Temperatures, Boosting Wildlife Survival Worldwide
trees_buffer_animals.summary: A global meta‑analysis shows tree cavities stay 3–4 °C cooler than ambient air, up to 15 °C in deep hollows, shielding animals from heat and cold.
highlights: Tree cavities worldwide are on average 3–4 °C cooler than outside air, with some up to 15 °C difference.
Analysis covered 36 studies spanning 65 years across five continents, focusing on the Global North.
Natural roosts outperform artificial bat boxes, which often exceed ambient temperatures and fail to retain night‑time heat.
Protecting large, old trees is recommended to mitigate mass mortality events during heatwaves.

helium3_quantum_computing.institution: Phys.org report on Helium‑3 quantum computing concept
helium3_quantum_computing.headline: Helium‑3 Enables Faster Quantum Tunneling for Next‑Generation Quantum Computers
helium3_quantum_computing.summary: Researchers at the University of Chicago propose using helium‑3 atoms trapped by optical tweezers to achieve tunneling rates three times faster than lithium‑based designs.
highlights: Helium‑3 atoms can be laser‑cooled and trapped with high‑powered optical tweezers
Fermionic helium‑3 offers native error‑resilient qubits versus bosonic helium‑4
Tunneling speeds are projected to be roughly three‑fold faster than lithium‑6 systems

perovskite_triple_junction_27_3_efficien.headline: Bilayer Strategy Boosts All‑Perovskite Triple‑Junction Solar Cells to 27.3% Efficiency
perovskite_triple_junction_27_3_efficien.summary: A graphene‑oxide and SAM bilayer devised by Helmholtz‑Zentrum Berlin lifts all‑perovskite triple‑junction cells to a record 27.3% efficiency with unprecedented stability.
highlights: Bilayer of graphene oxide and MeO‑2PACz suppresses optical and electrical losses at buried interfaces
Standalone tin‑lead sub‑cell reaches 22.1% efficiency, far above the 12.0% of SAM‑only devices
Triple‑junction stack attains 27.3% power conversion efficiency and retains 90% performance after 770 h
New interface enables 10.3 mA cm⁻² short‑circuit current in the near‑infrared bottom cell

bone_switch_ap503.headline: Leipzig Researchers Identify GPR133 Switch That Boosts Bone Strength
bone_switch_ap503.summary: A new compound, AP503, activates the GPR133 receptor in mice, markedly increasing bone strength while reducing bone loss, offering a promising osteoporosis therapy.
highlights: AP503 stimulates GPR133, an adhesion G protein‑coupled receptor, to enhance bone formation in healthy and osteoporotic mice
Activation shifts the balance toward osteoblast activity and away from osteoclast‑mediated resorption
The same compound also improves skeletal muscle strength, suggesting dual benefits for aging adults
Findings are published in the peer‑reviewed journal Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy (2025)

grb_boat_einstein.headline: Ultra‑high‑energy photon from GRB 221009A may have defied Einstein
grb_boat_einstein.summary: A record‑breaking gamma‑ray burst photon traveled two billion light‑years, apparently bypassing expected interactions with the cosmic microwave background.
highlights: The photon was detected by the Carpet detector at Baksan Observatory on Oct 9 2022.
Its energy exceeds any previously observed from a gamma‑ray burst, challenging standard photon‑CMB attenuation models.
Researchers propose axion‑like particle conversion combined with Lorentz‑invariance violation to explain its survival.
The theory predicts the high‑energy photon arriving about one hour after lower‑energy emissions, matching observations.
The study is on arXiv and accepted by Physical Review Letters.

moon_formation_5h_simulation.headline: Moon Could Have Formed in Just Five Hours, New Simulations Show
moon_formation_5h_simulation.summary: Researchers using temperature‑dependent material‑strength models find the Earth‑Theia impact might have produced the Moon in as little as five hours.
highlights: Simulations incorporated the hardness of Earth and Theia’s molten exteriors, a factor previously ignored.
Under the hottest temperature scenario, the Moon coalesced within five hours after impact.
The study appears in The Astrophysical Journal Letters (Sept. 1, 2026) and was led by Adeene Denton of Southwest Research

crawford_lake_ancient_dna_1000yr_record.headline: Ancient DNA Uncovers Millennial Human Impact at Crawford Lake
crawford_lake_ancient_dna_1000yr_record.summary: Sedimentary ancient DNA from Crawford Lake reveals a thousand‑year record of ecosystem shifts driven by Indigenous agriculture, European logging, and industrial pollutants.
highlights: sedaDNA captured plants, animals, bacteria and fungi across a 1,000‑year timeline
First detection of maize and sunflower DNA confirming Indigenous farming
Cattle DNA appears in early‑1800s sediments, unseen in traditional records
Capture enrichment with PaleoChip Arctic v1.0 enabled multi‑kingdom analysis

topological_magnets.headline: Layer Number Controls Magnetism in New Topological Ferrimagnet Ce₃Au₄Ge₂Bi₄
topological_magnets.summary: Researchers at Tohoku University demonstrated that adding spacer layers to square‑net crystals switches antiferromagnetism to ferrimagnetism while preserving Dirac electronic states.
highlights: Synthesized previously unknown two‑layer compound Ce₃Au₄Ge₂Bi₄ linking single‑layer CeAuBi₂ and infinite‑layer CeAu₂Ge₂.
Neutron scattering revealed ferrimagnetic order in Ce₃Au₄Ge₂Bi₄ versus antiferromagnetic order in the single‑layer analogue.
Calculations and high‑field measurements show a type‑II tilted Dirac cone unique to the two‑layer material.
The approach extends homologous‑series design to topological quantum materials, offering a systematic route for spintronic

rocky_tibetan_teleconnection.headline: Tibetan Plateau Heat Triggers Record Rainfall on U.S. West Coast
rocky_tibetan_teleconnection.summary: Unusually warm early‑winter temperatures on the Tibetan Plateau sparked atmospheric river intensification, causing record‑breaking rains in California and neighboring states in 2017 and 2023.
highlights: Tibetan Plateau temperatures were anomalously high in December 2016 and February 2023.
The resulting Rossby wave train amplified atmospheric rivers, delivering record precipitation to California, Nevada, Oregon
The extreme events caused about $6.6 billion in damages and at least nine fatalities.
Forecast models that rely on oceanic cues like El Niño missed the events, highlighting a new teleconnection.
Study published in Science Advances uses observations and simulations; first to link land‑surface heating to West‑Coast extreme

physics_aware_benchmark_thermal_conducti.headline: Physics‑Aware Benchmark Shows Why Similar AI Models Predict Thermal Conductivity Differently
physics_aware_benchmark_thermal_conducti.summary: A new benchmark from Columbia quantifies how machine‑learning interatomic potentials capture atomic vibrations, revealing why models with alike energy accuracy can diverge on thermal conductivity predictions.
highlights: Benchmark adds a physics‑aware metric based on atomic vibrational forces, not just formation energy.
Tested over 100 crystalline materials, exposing models that succeed by error cancellation.
Adopted by Meta, Microsoft, Radical AI, Orbital Materials, and integrated into Matbench Discovery.
With modest material‑specific training, predictions match reference calculations within a few percent, including lithium bromide

tiny_salt_crevices_martian_microbes.institution: ELTE Eötvös Loránd University / Konkoly Observatory
tiny_salt_crevices_martian_microbes.headline: Salt Crystals May Form Tiny Greenhouses for Martian Microbes
tiny_salt_crevices_martian_microbes.summary: Researchers propose that microscopic salt crevices on Mars could trap liquid brine and shield microbes, creating brief habitable windows each day.
highlights: Halite (NaCl) crystals can contract up to 1.6% between 150 K and 300 K, opening micro‑fractures at night
Deliquescence allows salts to absorb atmospheric moisture, forming brine when temperatures rise above 0 °C
Earth analogues show cyanobacteria thriving inside halite pores in the Atacama Desert

titanosaur_egg_site.headline: Titanosaur Eggs Reveal High‑Latitude Nesting in Southern Patagonia
titanosaur_egg_site.summary: A trove of 255 fossil eggshell fragments shows giant titanosaurs nested at 55‑60°S in Patagonia, using buried, heat‑producing nests.
highlights: 255 eggshell fragments from the Chorrillo Formation were identified as Fusioolithus, a titanosaur egg type.
Nesting occurred at 55‑60° south latitude with estimated temperatures of 12‑14.5 °C.
High pore density suggests eggs were buried in vegetation mounds that generated heat through decomposition.
Study led by Kohei Tanaka at University of Tsukuba and published in Royal Society Open Science (2026).

uv_breakdown_forever_chemicals.headline: UV Treatment Breaks Down PFAS into Fluoride, Offering a Clear Cleanup Roadmap
uv_breakdown_forever_chemicals.summary: University of California‑Riverside researchers detail how ultraviolet light converts persistent PFAS pollutants into harmless fluoride ions, guiding improved water treatment methods.
highlights: UV light and sulfite generate reactive electrons that cleave carbon‑fluorine bonds in PFAS
Fluoride ions are released as the primary byproduct, a far less hazardous form
Formate is identified as the main carbon‑containing product, correcting earlier assumptions

vlbi_690ghz_fringe_detection.headline: ALMA Achieves First 690 GHz VLBI Fringe Detection with APEX
vlbi_690ghz_fringe_detection.summary: On 21 Nov 2024, ALMA’s new Band 9 phasing system captured a ~12‑SNR fringe on the 690 GHz baseline to APEX, marking the highest‑frequency ground VLBI achieved.
highlights: Fringes detected on the ALMA‑APEX baseline at 690 GHz with signal‑to‑noise ratio ≈12
ALMA’s Band 9 phasing remained stable for 1‑2 minutes before degrading
No fringes on the ALMA‑JCMT baseline despite excellent weather, matching sensitivity forecasts

gw_lensing_lowfreq_universal_connection.headline: Universal Link Found Between Lens Density Profiles and Low‑Frequency Wave Optics in Gravitational‑Wave Lensing
gw_lensing_lowfreq_universal_connection.summary: Researchers derive how the low‑frequency amplification factor reveals the density profile of gravitational lenses, distinguishing spherical and power‑law tails.
highlights: Low‑frequency expansion of the amplification factor is expressed in powers of frequency under the Born approximation
Spherically symmetric lenses show only logarithmic dependence in the leading term, tied to density‑profile moments
Power‑law tail profiles introduce fractional‑power and logarithmic terms reflecting asymptotic density behavior
Quadrupole contributions appear only as higher‑order corrections in the low‑frequency regime

j1852_starforming_pevatron.headline: LHAASO Detects 1LHAASO J1852+0050u Gamma Rays Linked to Star‑Forming Region
j1852_starforming_pevatron.summary: Analysis of four years of LHAASO data and sixteen years of Fermi‑LAT observations shows the extended 1LHAASO J1852+0050u source likely powered by a nearby star‑forming region.
highlights: 1LHAASO J1852+0050u detected with ~13σ significance and 0.35° radius.
Coincident GeV source SrcAG identified in Fermi‑LAT data, matching the LHAASO emission.
Molecular clump linked to ultra‑compact HII region G34.26+0.15 at ~3.3 kpc provides target material for p‑p interactions.
Pulsar PSR J1853+0056 cannot account for the observed gamma‑ray flux.
Emission likely arises from protons accelerated by protostars (GeV) and massive stars (TeV) in the star‑forming region.

crocodile_sidm_dmdg.headline: SIDM Simulations Reveal Dual Role in Dark Matter‑Deficient Galaxy Formation
crocodile_sidm_dmdg.summary: New CROCODILE‑SIDM simulations show that self‑interacting dark matter can both aid and impede the creation of dark matter‑deficient dwarf galaxies, depending on their inner density profile.
highlights: Self‑interacting dark matter (SIDM) alters dark matter retention between pericentric passages of dwarf satellites.
A cuspy NFW initial profile loses more dark matter with higher SIDM cross sections, while a cored Burkert profile retains more.
The opposing effects stem from SIDM heat conduction direction, driven by the halo’s evolutionary state at infall.

hybrid_spin_orbit_tomography.headline: Hybrid Spin‑Orbit Tomography Maps Earth‑Like Exoplanet Surfaces and Clouds
hybrid_spin_orbit_tomography.summary: A new Hybrid Spin‑Orbit Tomography technique extracts static surfaces and dynamic cloud patterns from multicolor light curves, validated on Earth data.
highlights: Simultaneous retrieval of static surface maps and a single dynamic cloud component from photometric variability
Applied to DSCOVR/EPIC Earth observations, recovering oceans, vegetation, and land signatures
Hybrid model reduces residual scatter compared to static spin‑orbit unmixing
Uses sparse, volume, and Kronecker‑sum kernel regularizations for robust inversion

2609_10128v1.headline: CTA Observatory to Pinpoint Hadronic Gamma‑Ray and Neutrino Signals from Nearby Blazars
2609_10128v1.summary: A study shows that ultra‑high‑energy cosmic rays in four bright blazars produce a modest gamma‑ray component but a strong neutrino output detectable by CTA and neutrino telescopes.
highlights: Cosmogenic gamma rays contribute up to ~7.5% of the highest‑energy gamma‑ray emission
Neutrino luminosities range from 10^44 to 10^46 erg s⁻¹ for the four sources
CTA simulations of 50‑hour exposures can reconstruct intrinsic spectra and constrain hadronic models

dark_galaxy_cloud9.headline: Ultra‑deep imaging finds no stars in candidate dark galaxy Cloud‑9
dark_galaxy_cloud9.summary: Astronomers using HiPERCAM on the Gran Telescopio Canarias set a 31.4 mag arcsec⁻² limit, revealing that Cloud‑9 contains at most 16,000 solar masses of stars.
highlights: HiPERCAM five‑filter observations reached a limiting surface brightness of 31.4 mag arcsec⁻²
Upper limit of 16,000 solar masses of stars within a 4,200‑light‑year region
Gas mass of ~1 million solar masses makes gas at least 60 times more abundant than any stars

denisovan_cave.institution: Chinese Academy of Sciences et al.
denisovan_cave.headline: Denisovan Hunting and Adaptation Unveiled in China’s Bianfu Cave Over 120,000 Years
denisovan_cave.summary: A new Nature study reveals that Denisovans occupied Bianfu Cave in Yunnan Province from roughly 190,000 to 70,000 years ago, leaving fossils, tools and hunted animal remains.
highlights: Denisovan fossils dated to 167,000‑134,000 years ago using luminescence and uranium‑series methods
Over 1,300 stone and bone tools show flexible technology and large‑prey hunting
Pollen records indicate a stable conifer forest habitat through shifting glacial periods

ai_pinpoints_when_fish_reach_their_therm.headline: AI System Detects Fish Thermal Collapse with Precision
ai_pinpoints_when_fish_reach_their_therm.summary: A new AI combines DeepLabCut and ResNet34 to automatically pinpoint loss‑of‑equilibrium in fish, enabling objective temperature‑tolerance measurements for climate‑change studies.
highlights: DeepLabCut tracks seven keypoints on each fish to monitor posture
ResNet34 classifies video frames to flag loss‑of‑equilibrium events
Across 50 individuals the AI matched expert accuracy and reproducibility

skyrmion_topology_optical_communications.headline: Optical Skyrmions Prove Robust Against Atmospheric Turbulence for Long‑Distance Communications
skyrmion_topology_optical_communications.summary: Researchers at the University of the Witwatersrand demonstrated that topological skyrmion structures in light retain their integer winding numbers even after traversing a 270‑metre turbulent free‑space link.
highlights: Created optical skyrmions with skyrmion numbers 1‑3 using a 532 nm laser, spatial light modulator and modified Mach–Zehnder
Measured unchanged skyrmion numbers through real‑world atmospheric conditions ranging from calm mornings to intense midday
Quantum experiment showed entangled photon OAM skyrmion (number 1) remained topologically stable despite turbulence‑induced
Both classical and quantum results suggest topology can serve as a protected information carrier for free‑space and satellite

sun_fingerprints_planet_engulfment.headline: Sun May Bear Chemical ‘Fingerprints’ From Swallowed Super‑Earth, Study Suggests
sun_fingerprints_planet_engulfment.summary: A new MESA model indicates that a planet five‑to‑ten times Earth’s mass could have been engulfed by the young Sun, leaving detectable interior signatures.
highlights: Researchers propose a super‑Earth‑sized planet was ingested by the Sun early in its history
The model simultaneously resolves helioseismic sound‑speed discrepancies and the Sun’s low lithium abundance
Predicted chemical and structural signatures could be identified through future helioseismic observations

ryugu_nitrogen.headline: Ryugu Dust Shows Nitrogen Concentrated into Complex Molecules Over Time
ryugu_nitrogen.summary: Analysis of two Ryugu dust grains reveals that nitrogen, trapped as ammonium and carbon‑nitrogen species, became increasingly concentrated as water evaporated from the asteroid.
highlights: Ammonium and carbon‑nitrogen compounds were found embedded in clay minerals and sodium carbonate
The nitrogen species cluster around sodium carbonate, indicating late‑stage brine concentration
Similar ammonium‑bearing clays were identified in NASA’s OSIRIS‑REx samples from Bennu

dark_energy_evolution_3000_sne.headline: Nearly 3,000 Type Ia Supernovas Suggest Dark Energy May Evolve
dark_energy_evolution_3000_sne.summary: A new catalog of almost 3,000 type Ia supernovas combined with DES data indicates dark energy’s influence could be weakening over cosmic time.
highlights: The catalog compiles ~3,000 type Ia supernovae observed over three decades.
Analysis incorporates gravitational lensing, cosmic dust corrections, and galaxy‑mass effects.
Results align with 2024 DESI findings that hinted at a time‑varying dark energy component.

1000_times_faster_operations_bring_relia.headline: Chalmers Researchers Achieve 1,000‑Fold Faster Quantum Operations Using Bosonic Codes
1000_times_faster_operations_bring_relia.summary: A new single‑cycle method developed at Chalmers University of Technology accelerates bosonic quantum operations by over a thousand times, moving fault‑tolerant quantum computing nearer.
highlights: Quantum lattice gates enable complex operations in a single driving cycle
The technique works on existing superconducting quantum circuit platforms
Potential to reduce error rates and speed up fault‑tolerant quantum computers

lunar_foundation_model_launch.headline: NASA‑IBM Lunar Foundation Model promises unprecedented moon surface maps
lunar_foundation_model_launch.summary: A new open‑source AI system unifies multimodal lunar data, delivering finer crater, ice, and volcanic feature maps for upcoming missions.
highlights: Lunar Foundation Model (LFM) integrates optical, laser, radar, and spectrometer data across 2 million map tiles
LFM outperforms SwinV2‑B by up to 19% in crater detection using half the training labels
Ice prospectivity errors drop up to 22% compared with previous models
Model and benchmark dataset SomBench are released on Hugging Face for community use

continuous_black_hole_radio_video.headline: AI‑Powered Video Reveals Blazar 3C 345 Jets Defy Shock‑Wave Theory
continuous_black_hole_radio_video.summary: A new AI algorithm called kine turns 27 years of VLBI data on blazar 3C 345 into a continuous video, showing bright knots move with the plasma rather than as faster shock waves.
highlights: kine reconstructs a 27‑year video from 116 VLBA observations with four‑times higher resolution
bright knots in 3C 345 travel at speeds comparable to the surrounding relativistic jet
polarization data indicate knots are magnetically energized, not shock‑compressed regions

rewetting_peatlands_may_curb_warming_dri.headline: Rewetting Peatlands Could Slash Temperature‑Driven CO₂ Emissions
rewetting_peatlands_may_curb_warming_dri.summary: A global analysis of 276 site‑years shows that raising water tables to within 20 cm of the surface markedly reduces peatland CO₂ releases under warming.
highlights: CO₂ emissions rise sharply when water tables fall below 60–75 cm and temperatures increase
Water tables at 20 cm or higher dampen the temperature‑driven CO₂ surge
Daily data from 113 site‑years confirm that higher water levels curb short‑term temperature sensitivity

mercury_shrinking_faster.headline: Mercury May Have Shrunk Up to 23 km Since Forming, New Study Finds
mercury_shrinking_faster.summary: A new analysis suggests Mercury’s radius decreased by as much as 23 km—10‑30 percent more than earlier estimates—due to hidden impact‑debris effects.
highlights: Mercury’s shrinkage could be up to 23 km, roughly 30 percent greater than prior models
Researchers used MESSENGER data to map surface roughness and reveal obscuring debris
The finding implies a larger metallic core, possibly altering estimates of core composition
BepiColombo will soon test these results with higher‑resolution observations

2609_11306v1.headline: New General Formula Links Primordial Black Hole Clustering to Non‑Gaussianity
2609_11306v1.summary: Researchers present an analytical expression for the PBH two‑point correlation function that works for any local‑type non‑Gaussianity, connecting clustering to the primordial trispectrum.
highlights: Derives a universal PBH bias parameter valid for arbitrary local non‑Gaussianity
Applies the framework to ultra‑slow‑roll inflation, curvaton and modulated reheating scenarios
Extends to broad power spectra, enabling cross‑mass‑scale correlation analysis

desi_baryoncdm_2026_09_11.headline: DESI Tightens Limits on Baryon‑CDM Perturbations, Dark Energy Preference Holds
desi_baryoncdm_2026_09_11.summary: Using DESI full‑shape data, researchers place tight constraints on baryon‑cold‑dark‑matter density and velocity biases, confirming that dark‑energy evolution signals remain unchanged.
highlights: b_{\delta_{bc}}=5\pm6 and b_{v^2_{bc}}=-0.031\pm0.023 for the LRG2 sample in a DESI‑only analysis
Switching to a w_0w_aCDM model yields b_{\delta_{bc}}=2\pm5 and b_{v^2_{bc}}=-0.032\pm0.022
Adding velocity‑divergence bias gives b_{\theta_{bc}}≈-760 with large uncertainty
Constraints on w_0 and w_a are virtually identical after marginalizing over baryon‑CDM modes

2609_10661v1.headline: Dark Matter‑Baryon Separability Framework Predicts Dynamics of Almost‑Dark Galaxy TTT J1237327+143535
2609_10661v1.summary: A new separability model links dark matter deficiency and baryon depletion, offering testable predictions for the dynamics of the ultra‑faint galaxy TTT J1237327+143535.
highlights: Extends the Dark Matter‑Baryon Separability Condition to a branch describing preferential baryonic loss
Derives dynamical consistency relations involving σₗₒₛ, M_dyn, baryonic fraction, and mass‑to‑light ratio
Connects halo mass estimates to the expected globular‑cluster population in the Virgo Cluster

2609_11056v1.headline: New EFT Method Reconstructs Ultralight Axion Oscillations with Sub‑percent Accuracy
2609_11056v1.summary: Researchers have implemented an effective field theory approach that captures relativistic axion oscillations, achieving sub‑percent agreement with exact solutions.
highlights: First EFT‑based technique to resolve rapid axion oscillations
Wavefunction representation includes relativistic corrections
Computational speed rivals existing methods while improving precision

arxiv_2609_10696v1.headline: Primordial Black Holes May Experience Runaway Growth During Cosmic Reheating
arxiv_2609_10696v1.summary: New analytical models show that PBH absorption of plasma during reheating can trigger runaway mass increase, altering early‑universe black‑hole evolution.
highlights: Reheating dynamics modify the critical condition for PBH runaway absorption
Two regimes identified: growth during reheating or delayed growth after radiation domination
A composition law links mass‑growth mechanisms across successive cosmological eras

xrism_perseus_icm.headline: XRISM Maps Chaotic Motions in Perseus Cluster Core via Resonant Scattering
xrism_perseus_icm.summary: XRISM observations reveal that small‑scale random motions dominate the intracluster medium within the central 60 kpc of the Perseus cluster, challenging bulk‑flow interpretations.
highlights: Resonant scattering of the Heα w line shows central flux suppression and outer‑region enhancement
Velocity dispersion matches line‑broadening measurements, indicating turbulence‑dominated motions
Simulations favor isotropic or radial motions over tangential ones

fuzzy_dm_constraints.headline: Euclid data tighten fuzzy dark matter mass limits via dwarf galaxy globular clusters
fuzzy_dm_constraints.summary: Using Euclid Early Release Observations of dwarf galaxies in the Fornax and Perseus clusters, researchers constrain the ultra‑light dark matter particle mass to around 10⁻²² eV.
highlights: Globular clusters in Fornax show no orbital decay for particle masses m₍₂₂₎≤1.46⁺⁰·⁵¹₋₀·₃₂
Perseus clusters yield a similar bound of m₍₂₂₎≤1.09⁺⁰·¹₄₋₀·₂₁
The fuzzy dark matter model modifies halo density profiles and dynamical friction, alleviating the classic globular‑cluster

nonreciprocal_active_matter_2026_09_11.headline: Non‑reciprocal forces keep mixed colloids in perpetual motion
nonreciprocal_active_matter_2026_09_11.summary: Researchers at Tokyo University of Science discovered that size‑asymmetric electrohydrodynamic forces prevent aggregation, enabling continuous reorganization of mixed colloidal particles.
highlights: Mixed particles of 1 µm and 1.5 µm radii form asymmetric, self‑propelled pairs under an alternating electric field
Larger particles attract smaller ones more strongly, creating non‑reciprocal interactions that break apparent Newton’s third law
Clusters continuously fragment and rearrange instead of coarsening into static aggregates

arxiv_2609_10663v1.headline: Nautilus Space Observatory to Map Kuiper‑Belt‑to‑Oort‑Cloud Transition and Boost Cislunar Resilience
arxiv_2609_10663v1.summary: A two‑layer mission using a 4 m Nautilus Quattro Imaging unit and a network of ~50 cm telescopes will characterize near‑Earth small bodies while surveying distant Solar System objects to Vmag ~30.
highlights: 4 m Nautilus Quattro Imaging unit will conduct deep‑search surveys reaching Vmag ~30
~50 cm wide‑field telescopes in cislunar orbit will monitor meter‑ to decameter‑scale objects
Combined program aims to resolve fading planetary‑defense targets and map the Kuiper‑Belt‑to‑Oort‑Cloud transition

bh_galaxy_correlations.headline: GIZMO‑SIMBA and TNG‑Cluster Simulations Reveal Divergent Black‑Hole Growth Paths in Massive Clusters
bh_galaxy_correlations.summary: Zoom‑in simulations from GIZMO‑SIMBA and TNG‑Cluster show contrasting SMBH‑galaxy co‑evolution, with early torque‑limited growth versus delayed feedback‑regulated assembly.
highlights: GIZMO‑SIMBA predicts torque‑limited SMBH accretion that locks the halo‑mass–BH‑mass relation by z=3.0
TNG‑Cluster features early thermal suppression followed by kinetic winds that hard‑quench star formation
Both models reproduce the observed decoupling of BHAR and SFR in massive cluster ellipticals

distant_proto_supercluster.headline: Earliest Proto‑Supercluster COSMOS‑z3.1‑A Unveiled at Cosmic Web Intersection
distant_proto_supercluster.summary: Astronomers have identified COSMOS‑z3.1‑A, a proto‑supercluster seen when the universe was 2.1 billion years old, weighing about 5,000 times the Milky Way.
highlights: Mass of COSMOS‑z3.1‑A is ~5,000 times that of the Milky Way
Located at the junction of multiple filaments in the cosmic web
3D mapping used DECam, DESI, GMOS, and DEIMOS spectrographs

blue_light_breaks_rule.headline: Blue Light Defies Rule‑of‑Five, Unlocking 3D Drug Scaffolds
blue_light_breaks_rule.summary: A Bristol team used blue‑light‑driven photocatalysis to overturn the rule‑of‑five, creating rigid sp³‑rich bicyclic scaffolds for drug design.
highlights: Photocatalyst absorbs ordinary blue light and transfers energy to nitrogen‑containing 1,5‑dienes
Acetyl group on nitrogen directs regiodivergent cyclization, breaking the long‑standing rule‑of‑five
The method produced a 3D analogue of an experimental cognitive‑enhancement drug
Further functionalization shows the scaffolds can be diversified for medicinal chemistry

2609_10665v1.headline: Aletheia Emulator Delivers Percent-Level Halo Mass Function Predictions Across Dark Energy Models
2609_10665v1.summary: A new Gaussian‑process emulator predicts halo abundances with percent‑level accuracy for ΛCDM and a wide range of dynamical dark‑energy cosmologies.
highlights: Emulator uses evolution mapping to separate shape and evolution parameters
Trained on 100 flat ΛCDM simulations but applicable to curvature and quintessence models
Achieves per cent‑level accuracy over diverse masses and redshifts

pluto_atmosphere_collapse.headline: Pluto’s Nitrogen Atmosphere Shows 16% Pressure Drop, Hinting at Seasonal Collapse
pluto_atmosphere_collapse.summary: A uniform analysis of stellar occultations from 1988 to 2023 reveals Pluto’s lower atmosphere pressure fell 16% between 2022 and 2023, suggesting the onset of atmospheric collapse.
highlights: Pluto’s lower atmosphere pressure dropped 16% in 2022‑2023 after remaining stable since the 2015 New Horizons flyby
The decline was identified by re‑analyzing 10 new occultations alongside historic data from over 15 telescopes
Upper atmospheric haze cleared while lower‑atmosphere haze began to dissipate, indicating cooling and nitrogen snow formation

wasps_disappearing_summer.headline: British wasps vanish amid record heatwaves, scientists warn
wasps_disappearing_summer.summary: British wasps have become scarce this summer as unprecedented heatwaves and erratic temperatures threaten their survival and reduce adult size.
highlights: Extreme ground temperatures exceeded 50 °C, surpassing the wasps’ critical thermal maximum of ~45 °C.
The Big Wasp Survey has not yet collected data for 2026, leaving the decline anecdotal.
Remaining wasps observed are unusually small, indicating heat‑accelerated development and limited larval nutrition.
Researchers urge public participation in the Wasp Picnic Survey 2026 to gather observations.

2609_10622v1.headline: Variable Diffusion Ratio Resolves 2017 Cosmic Ray Depression Puzzle
2609_10622v1.summary: Researchers used AMS-02 data and a Parker transport model to explain the 2017 galactic cosmic ray proton dip by adjusting diffusion parameters.
highlights: The 2017 GCR proton flux drop coincided with strong CMEs as Solar Cycle 24 neared minimum
A steady‑state Parker framework matched AMS‑02 observations but gave unrealistic rigidity dependence
Allowing the perpendicular‑to‑parallel diffusion ratio to drop during CME activity restored expected turbulence behavior

pfas_to_silver_fluoride.headline: Electrical Pulses Turn PFAS Waste Into Recyclable Silver Fluoride
pfas_to_silver_fluoride.summary: Rice University researchers use flash‑encapsulated fluorination to capture fluoride from firefighting foam waste, producing silver fluoride for industrial use.
highlights: Flash‑encapsulated fluorination uses short electrical pulses to release fluorine from PFAS adsorbed on activated carbon
A porous quartz‑fiber barrier separates carbon and silver, preventing reduction of silver fluoride
The process removes >99.9% of fluoride, with 90% recovered as usable silver fluoride

mercury_magnetic_crust_2026.headline: Mercury’s Crustal Magnetism Mostly Explained by Present-Day Induced Fields
mercury_magnetic_crust_2026.summary: A new model using MESSENGER data shows that over 85% of Mercury’s northern crustal magnetic field can be accounted for by induced magnetization from its weak core field.
highlights: Induced magnetization can explain >85% of the crustal field north of 38° N
Magnetization strength correlates with crustal thickness up to ~30 km, not just iron content
Areas requiring remanent magnetization may reflect ancient asteroid‑delivered iron

ttr_aggregation_mechanism_2026.headline: Scientists Uncover Alternative Unfolding Pathway of Disease‑Linked Transthyretin Protein
ttr_aggregation_mechanism_2026.summary: Researchers at Scripps Research identified a second route by which the tetrameric TTR protein disassembles, potentially accelerating amyloid aggregation in rare hereditary forms.
highlights: Alternative pathway bypasses dimer intermediates, directly yielding monomers
Over 100 TTR variants were tested across urea and pH gradients
Cryogenic‑electron microscopy confirmed the expanded transition state
Pathway is favored in acidic lysosomal conditions and some brain‑associated mutations

wood_formation_climate.headline: Faster Wood Formation Trumps Longer Growing Seasons in Warming Forests
wood_formation_climate.summary: A global analysis of over 50,000 conifer samples shows that the speed of xylem cell production influences annual wood growth more than extended growing periods.
highlights: Rate of xylem cell production had a stronger impact on annual wood volume than season length
Warmer temperatures above ~6 °C slowed cell production, likely due to reduced water availability
Boreal forests benefit from faster growth, while Mediterranean and temperate forests see limited gains

martian_gullies_non_water_mechanism.headline: CO₂ Frost Fluidization Drives Active Gullies on Mars, Not Water
martian_gullies_non_water_mechanism.summary: New pre‑print analysis shows seasonal CO₂ frost, not liquid water, carves the rapidly changing gullies near Mars’ south‑pole Sisyphi Cavi.
highlights: Spectral data from CRISM and OMEGA show no 1.5 µm water absorption during spring melt
Geyser activity peaks before gully formation, ruling out the Kieffer geyser mechanism
CO₂ sublimation creates a lubricating gas layer that lets ice‑dirt slabs slide down slopes

foraminifera_spiral_flipping_evolutionar.institution: Researchers featured in Quanta Magazine article
foraminifera_spiral_flipping_evolutionar.headline: Global Foraminifera Shell Chirality Flips Reveal Hidden Evolutionary Sweeps
foraminifera_spiral_flipping_evolutionar.summary: A new synthesis of 56 million years of fossil data shows that sudden, worldwide switches in shell coiling direction likely mark rapid population sweeps of cryptic foram species.
highlights: Foraminifera shells switched coiling direction simultaneously across Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans
Pulleniatina obliquiloculata displayed rapid flips every few thousand years over the past 860,000 years
Genetic studies suggest cryptic species with slight fitness advantages can dominate globally, akin to viral variants

dense_galaxies_bubble_early_universe.headline: Dense Galaxy Overdensity May Have Carved First Reionization Bubble at z≈10.5
dense_galaxies_bubble_early_universe.summary: A group of 18 galaxies at redshift 10.5 observed by JWST’s JADES survey appears to create a ~6 cMpc ionized bubble, hinting at early cosmic reionization.
highlights: The overdensity contains 18 galaxies, four times the typical field density at redshift 10.5.
Lyman‑alpha transmission rises toward the core, indicating an ionizing bubble roughly 6 cMpc in radius.
Stellar masses and star‑formation rates are modestly higher than field galaxies but not extreme.

ai_hidden_proteins_nature_2026.headline: AI uncovers hidden GPCR-like protein TM184C that mediates intercellular bridges and autophagy
ai_hidden_proteins_nature_2026.summary: Researchers used AI to compare 214 million predicted protein structures, revealing the hidden GPCR-like protein TM184C that regulates cell‑cell bridges and stress‑response autophagy.
highlights: AI compared over 214 million predicted protein shapes to find hidden GPCR family members
TM184C localizes to intracellular vesicles and drives formation of microtubule‑linked cell bridges
Disrupting TM184C reduces intercellular connections and alters autophagy markers
Human TM184C rescued yeast lacking Hfl1, showing a conserved billion‑year function

new_ice_form_neptune_uranus.headline: New Hexagonal Superionic Ice Phase Unveiled, Illuminating Neptune and Uranus Interiors
new_ice_form_neptune_uranus.summary: Researchers recreated extreme planetary conditions in a diamond‑anvil cell, discovering a hexagonal close‑packed superionic ice that may reshape models of ice‑giant interiors.
highlights: Ice adopts a hexagonal close‑packed (hcp) oxygen lattice above 200 GPa and 1,800 K
The hcp phase replaces the previously known face‑centered cubic (fcc) superionic ice
Experiments used laser heating and X‑ray diffraction at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility

sma_muscle_loss_drug_approval.headline: FDA Approves Isembyld, First Therapy Targeting Muscle Loss in SMA
sma_muscle_loss_drug_approval.summary: Scholar Rock’s Isembyld received FDA approval for adults and children with SMA, showing significant motor skill gains when added to SMN2‑targeting treatments.
highlights: Isembyld approved by the FDA for patients aged 2 years and older
First drug to inhibit myostatin and address muscle loss in spinal muscular atrophy
Late‑stage trial showed motor‑skill improvement versus decline in placebo

grass_genome_assembly_2026.institution: Donald Danforth Plant Science Center et al.
grass_genome_assembly_2026.headline: Chromosome‑Level Genome of Streptochaeta Rewrites Grass Evolution History
grass_genome_assembly_2026.summary: A chromosome‑level genome of the tropical grass Streptochaeta spicata reveals an ancient allopolyploid event that reshapes the early evolutionary timeline of all grasses.
highlights: Researchers assembled a chromosome‑level genome for Streptochaeta spicata, a basal grass lineage.
Comparative analysis shows the ancestral grass genome underwent an allopolyploid duplication.
The duplication signature persists in modern cereals such as rice, wheat, and maize.
Findings published in Nature Communications (2026) provide a new framework for crop‑genomics research.

interfacial_water_photocatalysis_tio2.headline: Weaker water‑TiO₂ bonds boost photocatalytic hydrogen production
interfacial_water_photocatalysis_tio2.summary: A study using infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry shows that weaker water‑TiO₂ interactions and flexible hydrogen‑bond networks enhance interfacial water reactivity for H₂ evolution.
highlights: Weaker water‑TiO₂ interactions correlate with higher H₂ evolution rates
More flexible hydrogen‑bond networks increase water reactivity
Infrared spectroscopy combined with real‑time mass spectrometry quantified interfacial water structure
Normalization by surface area and water layers isolated true catalytic activity

breast_cancer_pill_trial_failure.headline: AstraZeneca’s Breast Cancer Pill Fails Pivotal First‑Line Trial
breast_cancer_pill_trial_failure.summary: The camizestrant‑Etcamah combination did not extend progression‑free survival versus standard therapy in the SERENA‑4 trial of ER‑positive, HER2‑negative advanced breast cancer.
highlights: Camizestrant plus a partner drug was tested as first‑line treatment for advanced disease
The SERENA‑4 trial showed no improvement in progression‑free survival compared with standard care
The drug had received accelerated approval in the U.S. for mutation‑driven resistance

copper_uti_mechanism.institution: Texas A&M College of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences
copper_uti_mechanism.headline: Texas A&M Researchers Harness Copper to Combat Antibiotic‑Resistant UTIs
copper_uti_mechanism.summary: Scientists at Texas A&M are studying how the immune system’s copper surge attacks urinary tract infections and how bacteria adapt, aiming for new copper‑based therapies.
highlights: The body increases copper levels in urine during infection, creating a toxic environment for bacteria.
UTI‑causing bacteria possess copper‑detoxifying mechanisms but are vulnerable when copper is combined with immune antimicrobials.
Researchers identified an experimental antimicrobial that works better with copper and are modifying it for future therapies.

whole_body_cell_communication_imaging.headline: WHOLISTIC Imaging Reveals Whole‑Body Cellular Communication in Live Zebrafish
whole_body_cell_communication_imaging.summary: Scientists used the WHOLISTIC system to capture second‑by‑second calcium signaling across entire zebrafish bodies, exposing organ‑wide cellular interactions.
highlights: WHOLISTIC records fluorescent calcium activity throughout a living organism in real time
First applied to transparent larval zebrafish and adult Danionella cerebrum
Observed unexpected calcium spikes in chondrocytes during cold exposure and in meninges after ketamine
Captured brainstem‑driven redistribution of blood flow across the whole body

compost_microbe_enzyme_plastic_degradati.headline: Compost Bacterium Yields Enzyme That Breaks Down Polyurethane Foam and Nylon
compost_microbe_enzyme_plastic_degradati.summary: Researchers bioprospected millions of microbes from Kenya landfill, a tropical zoo, larvae guts and compost, uncovering a versatile enzyme that degrades tough plastics.
highlights: 12 enzymes identified, including 10 that degrade polyurethane and 2 that degrade nylon
The most promising enzyme, CC PUR1 from Chelatococcus composti, tolerates up to 80 °C and diverse solvents
Enzyme activity was screened using fluorescence‑activated cell sorting at up to 10,000 cells per second

fertilizers_and_extreme_heat_are_damagin.headline: Mississippi River Fertilizer Runoff and Heat Threaten Gulf Coral Reefs
fertilizers_and_extreme_heat_are_damagin.summary: Isotope analysis of coral cores shows that rising nitrogen from Mississippi fertilizer runoff, combined with extreme heat, has driven recent bleaching and disease in the Gulf’s Flower Garden Banks.
highlights: Over 60% of nitrogen in recent decades traced to the Mississippi River, peaking at 80% in 2023.
Heatwaves in 2016, 2022 and 2023 coincided with massive coral bleaching and disease outbreaks.
Coral skeletons recorded 270 years of nitrogen isotope changes, revealing the shift after 1850 toward anthropogenic sources.

shapeshifting_plant_roots.headline: Shapeshifting Plant Roots Balance Anatomy, Metabolism, and Microbes to Boost Survival
shapeshifting_plant_roots.summary: Researchers at the University of Nottingham discovered that root anatomical complexity and metabolic reprogramming enable plants to remodel roots when colonized by microbes under nutrient stress.
highlights: Root anatomical complexity dictates the ability to remodel in response to microbial colonization
Microbial presence triggers extensive metabolic reprogramming in plant roots
Findings were published in Nature Communications (2026)
Synthetic biology and N6,N6,N6-trimethyl‑L‑lysine could steer beneficial root‑microbe interactions

bat_dna_longevity.headline: Bats’ DNA Reveals Immune Tricks Linked to Exceptional Longevity
bat_dna_longevity.summary: Eight Myotis bat genomes show that heightened immune defenses and rapid cell‑death pathways may underpin decades‑long lifespans, offering clues for human aging research.
highlights: Long‑lived Myotis species possess elevated cancer‑fighting gene activity
Cells from the longest‑lived little brown bat trigger self‑destruction instead of DNA repair when damaged
Genes tied to bat lifespan overlap heavily with those governing viral interactions
Study published in Nature provides the first comparative analysis of eight Myotis genomes

ai_pathology_cancer_detection.headline: Human‑style AI Boosts Cancer Detection Accuracy on Pathology Slides
ai_pathology_cancer_detection.summary: A new AI trained on pathologists' search behavior achieved near‑perfect cancer spotting, outperforming generic models but still yielding notable false‑positive rates.
highlights: Pathology‑o3 identified cancer‑positive slides with 100% sensitivity, versus 87.5% for OpenAI o3.
False‑positive rate was 15.5% for Pathology‑o3, compared with 53.3% for OpenAI o3.
On an independent dataset, sensitivity remained 97.6% and false‑positives dropped to 37.1%.

rhobast_fluorescence.institution: Institute of Organic Chemistry (Ronald Micura group)
rhobast_fluorescence.headline: RhoBAST RNA Flip of G38 Triggers Fluorescence for Super‑Resolution Imaging
rhobast_fluorescence.summary: A single guanosine flip in the tiny RhoBAST RNA activates dye fluorescence, enabling rapid blinking and high‑resolution tracking of RNA in living cells.
highlights: RhoBAST adopts an inverted V‑shape that houses dye between two loops
Guanine residue G38 flips outward upon dye binding, creating space for activation
Fluorescence blinking from the nucleotide flip supports super‑resolution microscopy

feather_dinosaur_poop.headline: Feather Found in Dinosaur Coprolite Sheds Light on Bird Survival After Asteroid
feather_dinosaur_poop.summary: A 66‑million‑year‑old feather preserved in a Montana coprolite may explain why modern birds endured the impact winter that wiped out other dinosaurs.
highlights: The feather was recovered from a 66‑million‑year‑old coprolite discovered in the Hell Creek Formation of northeastern Montana
CT scans at USC revealed feather structure and associated scales and bone fragments from a hesperornithiform bird
Researchers propose that primitive feather insulation, not just aquatic habitat, influenced which bird lineages survived the

embryo_base_editing.institution: Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons
embryo_base_editing.headline: Base Editing Reaches All Cells in Human Embryos but Triggers Unpredictable DNA Damage
embryo_base_editing.summary: A Columbia study shows base editors can modify every cell in early human embryos, yet they also cause unpredictable chromosomal deletions and mosaic mutations.
highlights: Base editing achieved 100% allele transmission to daughter cells in single‑cell embryos
Unintended large‑scale deletions and off‑target edits were observed despite lower frequency than CRISPR
Mosaicism produced embryos with mixed genetic alterations, undermining clinical predictability
High mRNA levels of the editor halted embryo development, revealing dosage‑dependent toxicity

classical_light_quantum_machine.headline: LSU Turns Classical Light into Room‑Temperature Quantum Reservoir for Computing
classical_light_quantum_machine.summary: Physicists at LSU demonstrated that bright classical light, combined with photon‑number‑resolving detection, can act as a robust multiphoton quantum reservoir for information processing at room temperature.
highlights: The optical network accesses multiphoton states containing up to 40 photons
Photon‑number‑resolving detectors extract hidden quantum behavior from noisy classical light
The reservoir learned six distinct mathematical functions without reconfiguring the optical network

first_starburst_size.headline: New Simulations Reveal How Massive Early Universe Starbursts Could Be
first_starburst_size.summary: Researchers modelled primordial gas halos under intense Lyman‑Werner radiation, showing that late‑forming Population III starbursts could reach masses detectable by JWST with gravitational lensing.
highlights: Lyman‑Werner UV photons can suppress molecular hydrogen cooling, delaying collapse until atomic cooling triggers massive star
Simulations predict starburst masses large enough for detection when aided by strong gravitational lensing
JWST has already identified candidate galaxies with signatures of pristine starbursts far later than classic models expected

southern_ocean_carbon_sink_flip.headline: Southern Ocean Could Turn From Carbon Sink to Source Under Mitigation
southern_ocean_carbon_sink_flip.summary: New climate simulations show the Southern Ocean may switch from absorbing CO₂ to releasing it even as global emissions fall.
highlights: Simulations predict a net CO₂ release of about 8.6 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ under a net‑zero scenario and 8.5 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ under sustained
Warming surface waters and declining alkalinity reduce the ocean’s ability to dissolve CO₂, reversing the air‑sea CO₂ gradient
The model shows the flip occurring around year 2154, long after atmospheric CO₂ begins to decline

diamond_melting_point_correction.headline: Laser Shock Experiments Reveal Diamond Melts Over 1,300°F Lower Than Thought
diamond_melting_point_correction.summary: A new ultraviolet‑laser shock study shows diamond’s melting point is more than 1,300 °F lower, aligning measurements with theoretical models.
highlights: Diamond melts at ~12,140 °F (6,727 °C) under 660‑1,060 GPa pressures
The melt occurs without a solid‑carbon intermediate phase
Findings aid nuclear‑fusion capsule design and improve models of Uranus and Neptune interiors

atlantic_hidden_heat_valve.headline: Atlantic "Heat Valve" May Amplify Warming as AMOC Weakens
atlantic_hidden_heat_valve.summary: New research shows the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation acts like a heat valve, and its weakening could trap more heat, boosting global warming.
highlights: Researchers used three climate models that spontaneously generate D‑O‑like oscillations under glacial conditions.
Strong AMOC triggers deep North Atlantic convection, releasing large heat to the atmosphere and space.
Weak AMOC shuts down convection, causing heat buildup in the ocean interior and raising planetary energy.
The “heat‑valve” concept explains why Greenland records show rapid changes while Antarctic records lag.
Future AMOC weakening may amplify warming by throttling this heat‑valve, though modern ice‑free conditions differ from the

nepal_flood_cascading_hazards.headline: Glacier Collapse Triggers Deadly Flood in Nepal, Exposing Cascading Himalayan Hazards
nepal_flood_cascading_hazards.summary: A massive ice‑rock collapse blocked the Bhotekoshi tributary for 18 hours, then burst, killing over 1,000 people and highlighting compound mountain hazards.
highlights: Ice‑rock mass failure created a natural dam on the Lhende Khola tributary
Dam breach unleashed a fast‑moving debris flood that destroyed bridges, roads and hydropower infrastructure
Satellite imagery from Planet Labs and IRDR analysis reconstructed the cascade after the event

ozempic_aging_mouse_study.headline: Semaglutide Extends Lifespan and Reverses Aging Signs in Older Mice
ozempic_aging_mouse_study.summary: Semaglutide treatment in 20‑month‑old female mice prolonged median lifespan by nearly 100 days while improving memory, muscle function and aging biomarkers.
highlights: Semaglutide increased median lifespan by ~100 days in aged mice
Treated mice showed better spatial memory and muscle performance
Inflammation and tissue‑repair gene signatures shifted toward youthful levels
Effects exceeded those of a matched 24% calorie‑restriction diet

cyanobacteria_carbon_sequestration.headline: Tiny cyanobacteria drive majority of ocean carbon sequestration
cyanobacteria_carbon_sequestration.summary: New study shows two‑thirds of deep‑ocean carbon comes from tiny cyanobacteria, overturning the belief that larger phytoplankton dominate the biological carbon pump.
highlights: Sediment traps at 1,000 m in the South China Sea captured carbon linked to surface cyanobacteria
Amino‑acid carbon isotope signatures identified cyanobacterial carbon at depth
Aggregation and ballasting enable cyanobacterial carbon to sink with minimal loss

inflammation_switch_discovery.headline: UCL researchers uncover natural brake that speeds inflammation resolution in humans
inflammation_switch_discovery.summary: A human study shows that blocking soluble epoxide hydrolase boosts epoxy‑oxylipins, reducing intermediate monocytes and accelerating pain relief.
highlights: Blocking sEH with GSK2256294 raised epoxy‑oxylipin levels and cut intermediate monocyte counts
Pain resolved faster despite unchanged redness or swelling
12,13‑EpOME suppressed p38 MAPK, curbing monocyte transformation

sea_level_shorebird_habitat_2026_09_12.headline: Sea‑level rise threatens global shorebird habitats, study warns
sea_level_shorebird_habitat_2026_09_12.summary: A systematic review of 29 shorebird species shows rising seas and coastal squeeze could dramatically shrink critical feeding and nesting wetlands worldwide.
highlights: 78% of examined studies report negative habitat impacts
89% document declines in shorebird populations
Coastal infrastructure blocks wetland migration, intensifying habitat loss

venus_uv_dark_material.headline: Venus’s Pale Yellow Clouds May Hide Extremely Dark UV Absorber
venus_uv_dark_material.summary: Scientists have quantified how strongly the unknown absorber in Venus’s upper clouds must absorb UV‑blue light, sharply narrowing viable organic and inorganic candidates.
highlights: Absorption coefficient reaches ~1,278 cm⁻¹ at 375 nm across 365‑455 nm range
Model suggests a bulk liquid absorber would need ~10 g L⁻¹ if organic, or similarly high concentrations if inorganic
Future missions like the Rocket Lab‑planned Autofluorescence Nephelometer aim to test these constraints in situ

helium_abundance_precision.institution: University of Minnesota Twin Cities (and international collaborators)
helium_abundance_precision.headline: Record‑Precision Measurement of Primordial Helium Sets New Cosmology Standard
helium_abundance_precision.summary: An international team measured the universe’s primordial helium abundance to 0.5% uncertainty using 130 hours on the Large Binocular Telescope.
highlights: Helium abundance determined with 0.5% uncertainty, three times better than previous results
Observations focused on 15 pristine, chemically‑unevolved dwarf galaxies
The MODS spectrographs at the Large Binocular Telescope enabled simultaneous analysis of over 10 helium and 15 hydrogen lines

alzheimer_genome_layer.institution: University of California, San Diego (et al.)
