highlights: ARPESand spin‑resolved ARPES revealed opposite spin polarizations in split electronic bands of Co₁/₄TaSe₂.
The material avoids stray magnetic fields while generating spin currents, combining ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic
Experiments were performed at the Advanced Light Source and Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource, confirming theoretical

water_stable_catalyst.headline: Water‑Stable Ruthenium Catalyst Extends Olefin Metathesis to Living Cells
water_stable_catalyst.summary: A newly designed ruthenium catalyst with a cyclic (alkyl)(amino) carbene ligand remains active for up to 600 cycles in aqueous environments, enabling bioconjugation.
highlights: Ruthenium catalyst featuring a CAAC ligand shows unprecedented water stability
Integrated aniline group allows selective attachment to proteins and peptides
Catalyst retains activity for up to 600 reaction cycles in biological media

forests_drought_co2_absorption.headline: Drought Forces Forests to Lose Their Carbon‑Absorbing Power
forests_drought_co2_absorption.summary: When water scarcity forces trees to close stomata, photosynthesis halts and forests can switch from carbon sinks to net CO₂ emitters.
highlights: Forests normally capture about a quarter of anthropogenic CO₂ emissions
Each CO₂ molecule absorbed requires roughly 400 water molecules to be released
Severe drought triggers stomatal closure, halting photosynthesis and causing forests to emit CO₂
Species‑specific hydraulic vulnerability determines how quickly trees shut down water transport
Reduced transpiration can diminish regional rainfall, as seen in the Amazon basin

neurodegeneration_tcells.headline: Blocking CXCR3 Keeps T Cells Out, Slowing Mouse Neurodegeneration
neurodegeneration_tcells.summary: A Washington University study shows that an antibody blocking CXCR3 prevents T‑cell entry into mouse brains, reducing tissue loss by 40% and improving memory.
highlights: Antibody targeting CXCR3 stopped T‑cell accumulation in hippocampal regions.
Treated mice exhibited 40% less brain tissue loss in memory‑related areas.
Cognitive performance improved on standard memory tests despite unchanged tau levels.
Findings published in Neuron using preclinical mouse models of tauopathies.

polymer_tuned_perovskite_underwater_sola.headline: Polymer‑tuned perovskite solar cell achieves 34.71% efficiency at 10 m depth
polymer_tuned_perovskite_underwater_sola.summary: A Yunnan University team engineered a wide‑bandgap perovskite with polymer additive PHMG, delivering record 34.71% power conversion efficiency in simulated deep‑water light.
highlights: Wide‑bandgap perovskite tuned to 1.96 eV matches blue‑green underwater spectrum
Polyhexamethylene guanidine hydrochloride (PHMG) raises ion‑migration barrier from 0.07 eV to 0.21 eV
Underwater module generated 324 mWh at 10 m depth, powering LEDs in the South China Sea

iron_minerals_water_storage.headline: Iron Oxyhydroxide Minerals May Store Primordial Water Deep in Earth
iron_minerals_water_storage.summary: Newly identified iron oxyhydroxide minerals can hold up to 15% water by weight, offering a possible source for Earth's early oceans.
highlights: Minerals stable at core‑mantle boundary pressures exceeding one million atmospheres
Each mineral contains up to 15% water by weight, equivalent to a pint in a five‑pound piece
Dense enough to sink, they could transport water from the deep mantle to surface volcanic hotspots
Discovery published in Nature Geoscience provides the first concrete reservoir model for mantle water

microbial_profiling_method.headline: New Metax Profiler Cuts Through Contamination to Reveal True Microbial Signals in Low‑Biomass Samples
microbial_profiling_method.summary: A novel taxonomic profiler called Metax, developed by researchers at Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research, more reliably distinguishes genuine microbes from contamination in scarce‑DNA samples.
highlights: Metax uses genome‑wide read distribution to separate true signals from kitome artifacts
Improved identification and abundance estimates were shown across bacteria, archaea, fungi, viruses, and eukaryotes
Tests on human microbiome, wastewater and clinical samples demonstrated higher accuracy than existing profilers

salmon_genome_duplication.headline: Whole-Genome Duplication Drove Salmon Evolution Over 100 Million Years
salmon_genome_duplication.summary: A new EU‑funded study mapped gene activity in Atlantic salmon and rainbow trout, revealing how ancient genome duplication still shapes their development and traits.
highlights: The salmonid ancestor underwent whole‑genome duplication ~100 million years ago.
Researchers generated ~800 high‑quality sequencing datasets, totaling 80 billion DNA‑sequence pairs.
Gene expression is most constrained during late embryonic development, limiting evolutionary change.
The AQUA‑FAANG project, a €6 million EU collaboration, made the data freely available for future research.

pacific_water_paradox.headline: Pacific Thermocline Shows Paradox: Young Water Ages, Old Water Rejuvenates
pacific_water_paradox.summary: A simplified circulation model predicts that warming will slow vertical mixing, causing younger Pacific thermocline water to age while older deep water becomes younger.
highlights: Warming reduces density differences, weakening exchange between surface layer and thermocline at 200–1,000 m depth.
In the subtropical North Pacific, slower mixing makes the thermocline water older; in the tropical Pacific, it becomes younger.
The slowdown is linked to heat forcing from the Southern Ocean, affecting vertical velocities across the basin.

ocean_chemistry_life_breathing.headline: Ancient Ocean Chemistry Fueled Oxygen Rise After Great Oxidation Event
ocean_chemistry_life_breathing.summary: Researchers show that phosphorus recycling in early oceans created a feedback loop that kept atmospheric oxygen high for millions of years.
highlights: Phosphorus released from sulfate‑driven microbes boosted marine productivity
New mineral‑specific phosphorus analysis of South African rocks revealed bioavailable nutrient levels
The feedback loop sustained oxygen after the Great Oxidation Event ~2.3 billion years ago

room_temp_superconductor_scandium.headline: Scandium’s 3d Electrons Unlock Room‑Temperature Superconductivity in LaSc₂H₂₄
room_temp_superconductor_scandium.summary: Researchers at Jilin and Zhejiang Universities explain why LaSc₂H₂₄ superconducts at 43 °C under 167 GPa, pinpointing scandium’s 3d electrons as the key.
highlights: LaSc₂H₂₄ achieves a critical temperature of 43 °C at 167 GPa
Scandium’s 3d electrons reshape the Fermi surface, eliminating anisotropic superconductivity channels
Replacing Sc with Ca or Mg removes superconductivity, confirming the essential role of 3d orbitals

exoplanet_weather_simp0136.headline: Irish team uses JWST to decode weather on distant brown dwarf SIMP 0136
exoplanet_weather_simp0136.summary: Researchers at Trinity College Dublin applied a new Principal Component Analysis technique to JWST data, revealing temperature‑driven cloud structures shaping the atmosphere of the 20‑light‑year‑distant object.
highlights: SIMP 0136, a ~13 Jupiter‑mass rogue planet, shows three recurring weather states driven by temperature and cloud‑layer changes
Principal Component Analysis isolates dominant atmospheric patterns from minute brightness variations as the object rotates
The method, validated on high‑quality JWST observations from 2023, can be applied to other brown dwarfs and giant exoplanets

feathered_dinosaur_discovery.headline: Four‑winged dinosaur Norellraptor barsboldi sheds light on independent flight evolution
feathered_dinosaur_discovery.summary: A 57‑cm microraptor named Norellraptor barsboldi from the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation shows convergent flight traits, supporting multiple origins of avian‑like flight.
highlights: N. barsboldi measured 57 cm and died at three years old, preserving four wings and sharp predatory teeth.
About 30 % of 194 anatomical changes in microraptors parallel those in early birds, including a longer ulna than humerus.
The study, published in Nature Communications, shows the sequence of trait evolution differed between microraptors and Avialae.
Researchers Andrea Cau and team used comparative analysis to argue flapping flight arose independently in non‑avialan dinosaurs.

gene_therapy_huntington.headline: UniQure’s AMT-130 Gene Therapy Slows Huntington’s Progression Four Years Post‑Implant
gene_therapy_huntington.summary: Four years after brain implantation, UniQure’s one‑time gene therapy AMT‑130 reduced Huntington’s disease progression by 44% versus an external control cohort.
highlights: High‑dose AMT‑130 achieved a 44% slower decline in motor and cognitive scores
Benefit magnitude decreased compared with the one‑year follow‑up analysis
The difference did not reach statistical significance
Data derived from matched participants in a large natural‑history study

galaxies_cosmic_house_mirrors.headline: Webb Reveals Mirror‑Warped Galaxies in Distant Cluster MACS J0454.1‑0300
galaxies_cosmic_house_mirrors.summary: James Webb Space Telescope images show gravitationally lensed galaxies magnified over 300‑times, exposing structures from 800 million to 2 billion years after the Big Bang.
highlights: The cluster MACS J0454.1‑0300 lies at a redshift corresponding to when the Universe was ~8 billion years old.
Lensing by the cluster creates multiple arcs, revealing a galaxy group 2 billion years after the Big Bang and a single galaxy
Individual star‑forming knots as small as 5 light‑years are magnified by more than 300×.
Webb’s infrared sensitivity uncovers hundreds of galaxies missed by the 2014 Hubble image.
Data derive from JWST programmes #5058 (PI Furtak) and #6882 (PI Fujimoto).

haumea_core_2026.headline: Haumea’s Dense Rocky Core Unveiled by Satellite Dynamics
haumea_core_2026.summary: Analysis of two decades of Hubble Space Telescope astrometry shows the dwarf planet Haumea possesses a dense rocky core beneath an ice‑rich mantle.
highlights: Dynamical model fits Hubble astrometry to measure Haumea’s J₂ and satellite masses
Combined J₂ and occultation shape data confirm a rocky core overlain by ice mantle
Results suggest frozen‑in fossil figure but more data are needed

2609_35974v1.headline: JWST Survey of 29 Lensed Quasars Finds Hints of Self‑Interacting Dark Matter
2609_35974v1.summary: A study of 29 quadruply imaged quasars using JWST shows a strong preference for core‑collapsed halos, challenging the standard cold dark matter model.
highlights: Core‑collapsed halos favored with Bayes factors ranging from 6:1 to 24:1
Analysis spans halo masses from 10⁶ to 10¹⁰·⁷ M☉
Explaining the data without collapse would require unusually high globular‑cluster counts and excess subhalos

alpine_cristal_jwst_survey_high_z_resolv.headline: ALPINE‑CRISTAL‑JWST Survey Maps Dust, Gas and Stars in z~4‑5 Galaxies at Kiloparsec Scales
alpine_cristal_jwst_survey_high_z_resolv.summary: A new study combines ALMA and JWST/NIRSpec IFU data to resolve gas, dust and stellar distributions in high‑redshift galaxies, revealing varied metallicities and feedback effects.
highlights: Spatially resolved [CII] and dust continuum observations trace atomic and molecular gas across ~kpc scales
Oxygen abundance maps show 12+log(O/H) values of 8.1‑8.3 with up to 1 dex internal variation
Galaxies with strong outflows exhibit lower dust‑to‑stellar surface density ratios and reduced gas fractions
A revised [CII] conversion factor yields more accurate total gas mass estimates than previous calibrations
Some z~4‑5 galaxies possess dust‑to‑gas ratios an order of magnitude higher than local counterparts

2609_36632v1.headline: Unified Limits on Cosmic Neutrino Flux Across Ten Decades of Energy
2609_36632v1.summary: A new analysis combines data from Cherenkov telescopes, air‑shower arrays, and radio detectors to set 90% C.L.
highlights: Reconstructed energy‑dependent exposures from multiple experiments into a common all‑flavor ν+ν̄ framework
Applied a Poisson likelihood to merge event counts and backgrounds, yielding quasi‑differential limits
Used the combined exposure to constrain cosmogenic neutrino models and selected new‑physics scenarios

full_dataset_search_for_solar_wimp_annih.headline: ANTARES Sets Stronger Limits on Solar Dark Matter Annihilation
full_dataset_search_for_solar_wimp_annih.summary: Using data from 2007‑2022, ANTARES found no solar neutrino excess, tightening WIMP‑proton cross‑section limits for masses 35 GeV to 10 TeV.
highlights: Full ANTARES dataset (2007‑2022) analyzed for solar neutrinos
No significant excess observed over background
Upper limits placed on spin‑dependent and spin‑independent WIMP‑proton interactions
Limits improve previous ANTARES results by a factor of two‑three

crystal_spacing_magnetic_states.headline: Lattice Spacing Outperforms Electron Count in Predicting Magnetism of Complex Alloys
crystal_spacing_magnetic_states.summary: A study of Au‑based Tsai‑type approximants shows that the lattice parameter reliably predicts antiferromagnetic, ferromagnetic and spin‑glass states, surpassing the traditional e/a ratio.
highlights: Magnetic ground states align with lattice parameters: >14.72 Å (AFM), 14.62‑14.72 Å (FM), <14.62 Å (spin‑glass).
The inverse correlation between e/a ratio and lattice parameter was confirmed across Tb, Dy and Ho samples.
The unified magnetic phase diagram offers a practical roadmap for designing new quasicrystal‑based magnetic materials.

first_stars_simulations.institution: University of Bath, University of Chicago, Institut d'Astrophysique de Paris
first_stars_simulations.headline: MEGATRON Simulations Link First Stars to Cosmic Fingerprints Seen Today
first_stars_simulations.summary: New high‑resolution MEGATRON simulations show how the first stars illuminated the early universe and left chemical imprints still observable in ancient Milky Way stars.
highlights: MEGATRON combines radiation, chemistry and galaxy formation models in unprecedented detail
Simulations reproduce the chemical signatures that JWST observes in infant galaxies and that stellar archaeology finds in
Simplified models underestimate stellar radiation effects, missing key gas structures
The project secured 40 million processor‑hours on UK national supercomputers for future higher‑resolution runs

300tevphoton.headline: 300 TeV Photon from GRB 221009A Challenges Standard Physics
300tevphoton.summary: A photon‑like event of 300 TeV detected after GRB 221009A may require axion‑like particles or Lorentz‑invariance violation to explain its survival across the cosmos.
highlights: Carpet detector recorded a 300 TeV photon‑like event with only 3 × 10⁻⁴ chance of misidentifying a hadron
ALP conversion can aid photons up to ~20 TeV but falls short by two orders of magnitude at 300 TeV
Lorentz‑invariance violation could raise the photon‑photon absorption threshold, making the universe more transparent at

dinosaurseaweeddiet.headline: Dinosaur Teeth Reveal Seaweed Consumption Along Ancient North American Coastlines
dinosaurseaweeddiet.summary: Isotope analysis shows coastal dinosaurs and crocodiles incorporated marine macroalgae into their diets, confirming marine subsidization in Cretaceous ecosystems.
highlights: δ13C values in coastal fossil teeth are consistently higher than those from inland sites
Study examined fossils from early Albian (113–107 Ma) and early Cenomanian (100–96 Ma) deposits
Marine macroalgae identified as the most likely source of extra carbon across the food chain
Tenontosaurus tilletti showed no marine signature, indicating dietary variation

2609_35941v1.headline: JWST Finds Massive Pop III Galaxies Near GN‑z11 Analog, Shaped by Baryon‑Dark Matter Streaming
2609_35941v1.summary: A semi‑analytic model applied to a zoom‑in N‑body simulation shows that high streaming velocities allow late‑forming Population III galaxies to survive near the bright GN‑z11‑like galaxy.
highlights: Pop III and metal‑enriched star formation start earlier and at higher rates in the overdense region
Late‑forming Pop III galaxies appear near the central galaxy due to ionizing feedback and strong Lyman‑Werner radiation
Higher baryon‑dark matter streaming velocity (v_bc) preserves chemical pristine‑ness, enabling these galaxies, absent when v_bc=0
